# synesis-graph

## Description

Role in the ecosystem: **graph export** · version 0.13.1

Consumes the artifact of `synesis compile`, not the `.syn` files.

**The exported graph describes itself.** When syncing with a database (ArcadeDB or Neo4j), `synesis-graph` writes a `ProjectContext` vertex with the context of the project: the `DESCRIPTION` of the `.synp` and the whole template as a readable document (each field with type, scope, description, value scale and **GUIDELINES**), plus the graph edges with their direction.

A database schema is syntax without semantics: it says there is an `Aspect` vertex with a `name`, not that `Aspect` is an ordered scale or what each value means. Your `GUIDELINES` are your coding protocol. With them in the graph, whoever queries it (Claude Desktop, any MCP client, the database studio, a colleague with a copy) knows your criteria instead of guessing them.

To read it: `MATCH (p:ProjectContext) RETURN p.description, p.template_doc`.

## Usage

```text
SYNESIS GRAPH (v0.13.1)

Universal pipeline from Synesis projects to graph databases and visualizations.

Usage: synesis-graph [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGUMENTS]...

Global Options:
  -v, --verbose        Increase log verbosity (DEBUG). Repeatable.
  -q, --quiet          Decrease log verbosity (-q WARNING, -qq ERROR). Repeatable.
  --version            Show version and exit
  --help               Show this message and exit

Commands:

  Graph Backends
    neo4j                Sync project to a Neo4j database (bolt://)
    arcadedb             Sync project to an ArcadeDB database (http://)
    arcadedb-embedded    Sync project to a local ArcadeDB database (no server)
    html                 Render an interactive HTML graph visualization

  Local Database
    serve                Keep a local database running for chat clients

Run 'synesis-graph COMMAND --help' for options and examples of each backend.
```

For the options of a subcommand: `synesis-graph <command> --help`.
